system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller package materially departs from the Buyer playbook and should not be accepted as drafted. No Amelia Frost approval has been given for any fallback requiring her written authority.

| ID / Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m**; 20% is available only with Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying the draft. | **Reject and restore 25% / AUD 6m** — the proposed fallback is not authorised. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | **AUD 25,000** de minimis; **AUD 250,000** deductible basket, with only excess recoverable. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000** tipping basket, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject and insert Buyer thresholds** — Seller’s proposal substantially reduces recovery for legitimate aggregated losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims notified within **18 months**. | **24 months after Completion**; 18 months requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval. | **Reject and restore 24 months** — no approval exists for the shorter fallback period. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limit. | Separate regime: **100% cap**, at least **six years**, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject and create a separate Fundamental/Title regime** — ownership and capacity risk must not be treated as an ordinary warranty risk. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no adequate fraud carve-out is offered. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all** caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insist on the full non-waivable carve-out** — Seller misconduct cannot be contractually sheltered by the general limitations. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; no deemed data-room, register or prudent-search disclosure. | **Delete the general disclosures and require specific fair disclosure** — mere document availability does not fairly disclose a warranty exception. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion; any knowledge qualifier should use identified **Seller knowledge persons**, subject to reasonable enquiry, and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. | **Reject the actual, adviser and constructive-knowledge bar** — it improperly transfers disclosure and investigation risk to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Seller gives reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent, although no final consent or evidence of satisfying clause 11.3 conditions exists. | Effective consent **and evidence that all associated conditions are satisfied before Completion**. | **Make effective, unconditional Bluefen consent a Completion condition** — delivery alone and reasonable endeavours are inadequate for a customer representing about 30% of revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases of all security at Completion. | **Require simultaneous repayment and release at Completion** — a post-Completion release is unacceptable absent an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval, neither of which exists. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** Completion bonuses are treated as a Seller matter but omitted from funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unresolved. | A specific funds-flow line item or other clear Seller funding for the bonuses and all triggered on-costs. | **Itemise and Seller-fund the full liability** — omission creates a risk that the Company or Buyer bears a Completion-triggered Seller cost. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; DD-010 records **AUD 180,000** open but this is not independently verified. | Broader protection covering the Ironquay IP defect and resulting loss, while preserving the SOW3 payment/assignment cure; independently verify the amount and status. | **Broaden the indemnity and verify before relying on the cure** — payment alone may not address all ownership, assignment and exploitation risks, and AUD 180,000 is unverified. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; current evidence does not establish access, exact scope, notification duty or loss. | Preserve relevant logs and evidence, continue investigation, provide prompt updates and address any substantiated remediation or liability without prejudging the result. | **Add preservation, investigation and update covenants** — the facts remain unresolved, so neither a confirmed breach nor a clean bill of health should be assumed. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and avoidability; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction. | **Reserve position pending assessment** — the disclosure does not establish either ordinary-course treatment or a purchase-price adjustment. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Seller proposes that limitations applying to Claims apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded, and treats Tax/IP as settled under the general regime. | Separate regimes for Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants, with no hidden general-regime override. | **Reject the omnibus limitation language and specify each category expressly** — otherwise bespoke protections may be unintentionally capped or time-barred. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on the internal DD-012 share register as evidence of ownership of 100% of the shares. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrance status and authority, including appropriate searches, certificates, transfer documents and releases. | **Require independent verification and Completion evidence** — the Company’s supplied internal register is relevant but is not conclusive independent proof. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says Tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the proposed general regime. | Keep Tax and IP terms **open** for separate negotiation; assume neither unlimited liability nor any agreed resolution. | **Reject any assertion that these terms are settled** — no agreement exists and the general regime must not determine them by default. |
=== END ADVICE ===
